# Mandate in ten minutes

Mandate casts DAO votes from a plain-language policy: three model jurors post verdicts on chain, and a reactive contract on Lasna tallies them, runs the veto window and casts the vote on the governor's chain. Everything below is generated from `evidence/summary.json`, and `make verify` rebuilds it from public RPCs.

In the live run on Base Sepolia, Unichain Sepolia and Reactive Lasna, all 15 cases resolved with no stuck case and no failed callback: 7 votes cast, 2 vetoed by the owner, 3 held on an injection flag (2 planted attempts, 1 false positive), 2 held as splits (1 of them expired when its vote closed) and 1 given up because voting had closed before the veto window ended. 45 of 45 written opinions re-hash to the hash their verdict put on chain. The chain hops are quick (proposal to case open p50 1.4 s, n = 10); the free model tiers are the slow part (case open to third verdict p50 807.4 s, n = 15).

## Execution

Five of the 7 loops that ended in a vote, with every transaction. Lasna links go to lasna.reactscan.net. Times are from the proposal, each on its own chain's clock.

Check it yourself: `make verify` re-reads every receipt and log from public RPCs, rebuilds all 15 rows of `evidence/cases.csv`, re-hashes every opinion against its `Verdict` event, confirms each `modelIdHash` and `promptHash`, recomputes the timing and cost tables, checks Sourcify, and writes `evidence/verify-report.json`.

## Integration

- Trigger your own loop without a wallet: open https://mandate-omni.vercel.app/propose, pick a sample or write your own text, and submit. The site's relayer files it on the demo governor; the reactive contract opens a case within seconds and the Docket page (https://mandate-omni.vercel.app/docket) shows the three opinions, the tally, the veto countdown and the cast vote as they land.
- Reactive pieces in use: `ProposalCreated` subscriptions on four governors across two chains, the Docket's `CaseOpened`, `Verdict`, `Vetoed` and `Overridden`, the Delegates' `Cast`, `NotActive` and `Cancelled` acknowledgements, callbacks to two destination chains, and a cron subscription that is on only while a case is timed.
- Re-run a juror on a recorded case: `make replay CASE=<id> JUROR=<1|2|3>` checks the snapshots and hashes, re-runs the model and reports drift. 6 recorded replays: 4 reproduced exactly, 2 drifted.

## Usefulness

Who it is for: a token holder who will not read every proposal but can write down how they want to vote, and a delegate who wants a first reading of every proposal against a stated policy.

- Injection attempts are held, not voted: 2 of 2 planted attempts held (C03, C07). C03's verdicts were juror 1 against at 8500 bps with an injection flag, juror 2 for at 9000 bps with an injection flag, juror 3 against at 9500 bps with an injection flag: a juror can follow the planted text and still flag it, and the flag is what holds the case.
- The owner stays in charge: 2 vetoes stopped decided votes inside the window and 1 override cast the owner's choice on a held case; juror weights after the run are juror 1 75, juror 2 50, juror 3 50 (start 100).
- Evaluation on 72 real, already decided proposals under two mandates ([analysis/eval/MODEL_CARD.md](analysis/eval/MODEL_CARD.md), recomputed offline by `make verify`):

| Mandate | Proposals | All three jurors agree | At least two agree | Quorum decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `conservative-treasury.v1.md` | 72 | 36% (26/72) | 88% (63/72) | 2 for, 48 against, 7 abstain, 15 held split, 0 held by a flag |
| `growth.v1.md` | 72 | 2.8% (2/72) | 76% (55/72) | 22 for, 13 against, 9 abstain, 27 held split, 1 held by a flag |

The mandate changes the vote: the quorum decision differs between the two mandates on 75% (54/72) of proposals. Agreement with how the DAO actually voted is 26% (13/50) of decided cases under `conservative-treasury.v1.md` and 54% (19/35) of decided cases under `growth.v1.md`; a mandate is a personal policy, so that is how often this voter sides with the majority, not accuracy. The card lists where the jurors disagree and why.

## Craft

- Tests: 180 Foundry tests in 18 files (`make test`), 157 juror worker tests (`cd workers && pnpm test`) and 75 web tests with 2 skipped (`cd web && pnpm test`), all passing. CI runs them on every push with `forge fmt`, `forge build --deny warnings`, coverage, Slither, Biome, typecheck, the writing check and a full-history secret scan (`make ci` locally).
- Evidence tables, each with its n: 15 live cases in `evidence/cases.csv`, 45 verdicts with 45 matching opinions, the per-step timing below, and 144 rows in `analysis/eval/results.csv` and 144 rows in `analysis/eval/results_live-lineup.csv`.

| Step | Clock | n | p50 | p90 | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Proposal to case open on the Docket | Base, ms stamps | 10 | 1.4 s | 1.8 s | 1.0 s | 2.0 s |
| Case open to first verdict | Base, ms stamps | 15 | 63.2 s | 81.2 s | 14.2 s | 144.6 s |
| Case open to third verdict (quorum 3) | Base, ms stamps | 15 | 807.4 s | 1,137.8 s | 54.8 s | 1,174.2 s |
| Third verdict to veto window start on Lasna | Base ms to Lasna s, Lasna stamps run early | 9 | -0.6 s | -0.2 s | -1.4 s | -0.2 s |
| Veto window | Lasna s, configured 300 s | 9 | 300.0 s | 300.0 s | 300.0 s | 300.0 s |
| Window end to vote cast on the governor | Lasna s to governor chain | 5 | 39.4 s | 65.0 s | 5.6 s | 65.0 s |
| Proposal to vote cast, whole loop | Base, same clock | 5 | 1,066.0 s | 1,366.6 s | 361.0 s | 1,366.6 s |
| Third verdict to owner veto | Base, owner by hand | 2 | 27.0 s | 251.2 s | 27.0 s | 251.2 s |
| Proposal to case open on the Docket | Unichain s to Base ms, plus or minus 1 s | 5 | 1.4 s | 1.6 s | 1.2 s | 1.6 s |
| Proposal to vote cast, whole loop | Unichain, same clock | 1 | 1,255.0 s | 1,255.0 s | 1,255.0 s | 1,255.0 s |

- Limits, in full in [docs/LIMITS.md](docs/LIMITS.md); the ones that matter most:

- **Jurors are oracles.** A verdict is whatever a registered juror key signs. Quorum and `minAgreeing` 2 stop one key from moving a vote, but two colluding or identically fooled jurors can. The Docket owner chooses the jurors.
- **Independence is not enforced.** Verdicts are public once posted, so a juror could copy earlier ones; commit-reveal is not built.
- **One injection flag holds the case.** A proposer can bait the jurors into holding every case, and a single juror can stop automated voting by flagging everything. The owner releases a hold by override before voting ends.
- **Model drift and free tiers.** 2 of 6 recorded replays drifted from the recorded verdict, free quotas push jurors onto fallback models, and the model that answered is recorded per verdict rather than fixed.
- **Veto latency.** The window closes on Reactive time, so a veto sent in the last seconds can arrive after the cast request; the site stops offering the veto 20 s before the end.
